title: Stop web audio samples when stopping AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #100816

## Additional information

AudioStreamPolyphonic / AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic are used as the stream source when using AnimationMixer. 

Audio samples, used by default on web, get a lot of special treatment - there's many different codepaths for starting & stopping samples that differ from the rest of the engine. In order to properly clean up the samples started by AudioStreamPolyphonicPlayback, we need to explicitly stop the samples somewhere:

In almost every case, `AudioServer::stop_playback_stream` handles this by checking if a playback to stop is a sample; but in the case of AudioStreamPolyphonic: this stream is _not_ a sample stream regardless of if it's playing samples under the hood or not, and so this never triggers the samples cleanup as the other cases do.

A (I believe correct) call to `p_playback->stop()` was [added](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/97625), which is needed to fix #100816 - however, it was later found this this added call causes [some](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100819) [crashes](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100173). 

Peculiarly - `p_playback->stop()` was wrapped in a conditional in #101097 so that `p_playback->stop()` is only called if the playback is _not_ playing. 

Investigating some issue reports related to these changes, I believe `AudioStreamPolyphonicPlayback::stop` crashed the AudioServer due to a logic error causing AudioStreamPolyphonicPlayback::stop to take multiple AudioServer locks (one for each active stream), and only a single unlock.

I _think_ the original '[fix](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101097)' for the crashes was incorrect and just papered over the lock problems. There were not many details on the reasoning behind this change, and just reading it doesn't quite explain why, so I can't be sure.. 

I've removed this conditional preventing `p_playback->stop()` from being called if the playback is playing, and fixed the lock contention. This fixes #100816. 

I also confirmed calling `p_playback->stop()` unconditionally without the lock fix, that the audio driver indeed crashes very quickly using the [MRP](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100173#issuecomment-2552104766). After fixing the lock problems, the same MRP runs for a long time with no signs of crashing.

On web, this now-called ::stop method lets us clean up the audio samples that were started previously which stops the samples upon scene change. The explicit stop of samples is required here.. simply setting their finish_request doesn't get picked up in the existing cleanup in mix - ~I'm not totally sure why, I'm assuming mix isn't called after they're stopped? let me know if I missed something there and should have used the finish_request flag + some other change.~ nvm, stop sets active=false which short circuits mix, even if it were called. 

I checked other AudioStream* playback classes and from what I can tell all the *::stop methods look benign and i don't think would have a problem with this (and may even resolve this https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101097#issuecomment-2613042635 if it's still unresolved.) 

---

As there looked to be several issues related to this, both web and in general, I'd appreciate some testing. I've tried all the MRPs and it all seems to check out.

(purely human contribution)
